title: Organize Automation with Roles
objective: Package reusable tasks, defaults, handlers, files, templates, and dependencies as roles.

sourceAlignment.title: Ansible for DevOps, 2nd Edition
sourceAlignment.author: Jeff Geerling
sourceAlignment.chapterTitle: Playbook Organization - Roles, Includes, and Imports

paragraphs: Imports are resolved while a playbook is parsed; includes are dynamic and can respond to runtime conditions. Both split large automation into coherent files, but their timing affects tags and conditions.

A role follows a conventional directory layout for tasks, defaults, vars, handlers, files, templates, metadata, and tests. Defaults are intended for consumers to override; role vars have much stronger precedence.
Galaxy distributes roles and collections. Pin dependencies in a requirements file, install them locally to the project, review community code, and design roles around one clear responsibility.
explanation.rule: Put configurable values in defaults and keep each role focused on one responsibility.

examples.title: Pinned Role Dependency
examples.note: Pinning avoids unreviewed upgrades changing a build.
